shots.caption: Title page: author, workshop and date.
shots.quote: TEN YEARS OF CONCRETE SLEEPERS ON THE AUSTRALIAN NATIONAL RAILWAYS by R.J. Dixon

shots.caption: Sleepers installed to date, the 1780 km length and the sleepers still to be laid.
shots.quote: Reference to a map of Australia shows the Trans-Australian Railway extends from Port Pirie through Port Augusta to Kalgoorlie, a distance of 1780 km and the Tarcoola to Alice Springs Railway covers a distance of 830 km.
shots.quote2: The programmed rate of insertion for this project is 240 000-No. concrete sleepers per annum; some 1 470 000-No. sleepers or 980 km of track is still to be completed.

shots.caption: Timber sleeper density on the Trans-Australian Railway before the concrete programme.
shots.quote: At the time the railway track standard on the Trans-Australian Railway was 47 kg rails welded into 82 metre lengths on timber sleepers spaced at the rate of 1640 per kilometre. A light structure.

shots.caption: Concrete sleeper spacing adopted.
shots.quote: it was decided to adopt a closer spacing of 667 mm or 1 500 sleepers per kilometre.
